title: Pappardelle with Slow-Braised Pork Ragu
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless pork shoulder (Boston butt), cut into 2-inch chunks
1 medium onion, 1 carrot, 1 celery stalk (finely minced mirepoix)
1 cup dry red or white wine
1 can (28 oz) crushed San Marzano tomatoes
2 sprigs fresh rosemary, 3 sprigs thyme, 2 bay leaves
Freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano and chopped parsley
instructions: Season pork shoulder chunks generously with salt and pepper. Sear in a Dutch oven with 1 tbsp olive oil over medium-high heat until deeply browned on all sides; set aside.
Lower heat to medium and sweat the minced onion, carrot, celery, and garlic for 6–8 minutes. Stir in tomato paste and caramelize for 2 minutes.
Deglaze with wine, scraping up all browned fond, and reduce by half. Add crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, herb sprigs, and seared pork.

Cover and braise at a low simmer (or in a 300°F oven) for 2 to 2.5 hours until fork-tender. Shred the pork into the rich sauce, toss with al dente pappardelle and a splash of pasta water, and finish with Parmigiano-Reggiano.
